correctness.rationale: The canonical hyperelliptic two-to-one map over F5 gives at most two rational points above each of six base points; equality is exactly six nonzero-square value constraints. Interpolation proves precisely 320 coefficient candidates; exact gcd with the derivative proves 240 geometrically smooth and 80 singular. Direct exhaustive PGL2(F5) and square-scalar orbits have sizes 120,40,80 and sum to all 240, proving three arithmetic classes, with factors giving disjoint Frobenius types. Separate exact enumeration over two different representations of F25 yields point counts 26,28,24, fixing the Weil polynomials by Newton identities. Three runnable checkers and actual outputs are included. There is no incomplete infinite inference.

originality.rationale: The statement-level novelty assessed here is the exact classification of the maximal 12-point genus-two F5 locus into three arithmetic isomorphism classes with one-to-one Frobenius partition and full Weil polynomial. The twelve-point bound, generic hyperelliptic orbit method, and existence are explicitly prior work. Direct full-text inspections of three relevant OA primary papers and six actual published-finding corpus semantic queries found no matching joint assertion. A complete earlier arithmetic table could encode this result, so priority remains qualified and independently checkable.
residual_risks: A complete curve database or unpublished enumeration may already contain the 12-point subclass implicitly.
Cardona 2003 and a specialized 2005 F5m genus-two classification were not inspected in full text, so priority cannot be certified against them.
The classification is deliberately restricted to a single finite field and does not extrapolate to all odd fields.

value.rationale: The extremal 12-point locus is motivated by the sharp gonality bound; specifying which genus-two arithmetic curves achieve it is a natural finite-field moduli question. The trichotomy shows exactly three different closed-point patterns for their ramification divisors, and exactly three distinct Jacobian Frobenius polynomials, linking point maximization, hyperelliptic branch geometry, and isogeny invariants. It is a full arithmetic classification with numerical orbit/stabilizer and zeta data, not an arbitrary slice or mere recomputation of the upper bound. Its scope is finite and explicitly limited.
